## Description

Fresh native observation during SL-350 validation: a completed process-output offload remained I/O-parked indefinitely in the multithreaded irdet harness. This is not merely a long compile in the VM.

Run: sawlang-sl350-codegen, compiler92249ad8 on based2dc725e, tools/battery.sh, stage29 .build/irdetbin --all --python /Users/swoodtke/Projects/sawlang/.venv/bin/python --jsonl .build/irdet-battery.jsonl. Original irdet PID44324. JSONL stopped at1451 records (1307ok,144skip) at Unix1790168435.771. Task1451's 316813-byte result_discard_legal.ll was emitted at1790168435.600 and parses as a complete LLVM module. No compiler child remained in process observations. No success/exit status for that child is inferred from IR emission.

Separated live snapshots: main waits in TaskGroup.__await_slot_inner; all eight workers are in reactor poll/wake or scheduler mutex paths, not executing tasks. Slot4/gen182 is the sole unfinished slot, active=false, remaining=-1. Other seven slots are done. Root check_one state5 -> check_one_reuse state4 -> emit_ir state1 -> Command.output state4. Every wake=-1, every deadline0; all __io_tok values correctly name the live root wake word0x8d4e37ad8. No stale child-frame token was observed.

The decisive offload snapshot: Command.output's __blkjob0=0x8d4c480c0; function symbol __saw_blk_thunk$__saw_rt_proc_read_stdout; done=1, result=1 (one captured byte, NOT EOF), notification pipe_r=10/pipe_w=15. Args are the ProcJob, frame-owned buffer,1024. ProcJob has pid50959,stdout_fd17,wait_fd=-1. Thus the underlying read completed, but the coroutine never consumed it and remained parked. No target memory was changed or result consumed by the debugger; snapshots detached immediately. The original run was preserved during investigation.

Two independent read-only reviews found a concrete lost-latch candidate: blocking-call lowering registers readiness before _suspend_to writes -1; a concurrent poller can consume EV_ONESHOT and store0 through the root token, then nested Pending propagation copies a child's -1 back into root.__wake. There is no separate latch or preservation/CAS in that path. Source: coro_transform.py6736-6747,7876-7908,8140-8169; rt/host_macos/reactor.saw109-119,159-181; std/taskgroup.saw1531-1548,1567-1644. The exact historical interleaving is NOT proven; ignored registration failure remains an alternative. The protocol helpers build_resume, _suspend_to, _lower_stmt, _emit_blk_call and _emit_nested_call have identical Python ASTs between exact based2dc725e and candidate92249ad8. This is evidence of a pre-existing protocol candidate, not proof that SL350 cannot affect manifestation.

Do not interpret lsof's kqueue count1 as one registration: it counts queued events. The scheduler's events>0 self-wake and reactor USER-event cascade also admit a source-level feedback loop that can explain CPU activity without task progress; causality for this instance is not established.

Related SL-138 concerns a different cross-poller case: an ST poll that misses a correctly persistent latch. This observation is an MT group with bounded polling and a root latch still-1 after an offload completed.

Evidence retained in the codex session: sl350-scheduler-snapshot.json, sl350-scheduler-memory-snapshot.json, sl350-pending-frame-memory.json, sl350-pending-frame-decoded.json, sl350-offload-job-snapshot.json, sl350-irdet-frame-layouts.json, sl350-wakeup-base-source-comparison.json. No crashing baseline compiler or oversized-ABI reproduction was rerun. No workaround-assisted battery pass is claimed.

SWEEP REPORT (agent:claude-sl353-sweep, read-only, Sep 23; artifacts under `/Users/shawn/Projects/sawlang/.build/scratch/sl353/`; posted by the lead).

## Verdict
REPRODUCED, and the interleaving is directly instrumented. A lost-wake race in the SHARED io-park lowering, not an offload-specific bug: the reactor token (the ROOT frame's `__wake` word, handed down every embedded chain at `coro_transform.py:8149-8154`) is ARMED before the park value is written, and the nested `Pending` propagation then RE-STORES a child's -1 over a readiness 0 a concurrent poller already latched. `EV_ONESHOT` never refires and the bounded MT re-scan only re-READS the word (`taskgroup.saw:1585-1630`, ambient twin `:2150-2173`), so the task parks forever with its pipe readable and nobody registered on it. A detector that fires exactly when that store order occurs printed on 40/40 stalled runs and 0/184 clean runs. Registration FAILURE is excluded for every reproduced stall (probe C: `abort()` on any `kevent` arm < 0 — 4 stalls / 128 runs, zero aborts). The class covers `Command.output`'s offload AND every `std.net` park (both reproduced).

## Reproducer
`stress_proc.saw` / `stress_proc_wd.saw` (N-worker `TaskGroup(threads:)`, tasks looping `Command(program: "/bin/echo").output()`; the `_wd` twin has an OS-thread watchdog printing `dump_tasks()` then `_exit(99)`), `stress_net.saw` (`TcpStream.pair()` ping-pong, one end per task), drivers `run_wd.sh`/`run_par.sh`/`run_grid.sh` (`perl -e 'alarm N; exec @ARGV'` — macOS has no `timeout`). IT ONLY REPRODUCES UNDER CPU OVERSUBSCRIPTION (16 concurrent instances × 8 workers on 16 cores): serial `threads=8 tasks=1 iters=200 reps=100` → 0 stalls in 20,000 offloads — the window is the few instructions between the arm and the root store, so it needs a preemption there.

| build | shape | threads | runs | stalls |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| baseline | proc offload | 8 | 128 + 128 | 8 + 3 |
| baseline | proc offload | 4 | 96 | 1 |
| baseline | proc offload | 2 | 96 | 0 |
| baseline (ST control, 10× the work) | proc offload | 1 | 96 | 0 |
| baseline | net park (4 tasks × 20,000 rounds) | 8 | 96 | 4 |

Stall signature, identical in all captured dumps and to codex's snapshot: `task group 1 slot 0 gen 1 io-parked / at process.saw:555 in Command.output`; `sample` of the hung process: main in the join's `pthread_cond_wait`, all eight workers cycling `__saw_rt_reactor_poll`/`_wake`/the scheduler mutex (the USER-event cascade CPU burn). Net stalls park BOTH peers at `net.saw:1074 in TcpStream.read`.

## Ordering table (each cell read from code)
Registration funnel: `__saw_exec_io_register` (`sawc/std/taskgroup.saw:566-568`) → `rt_reactor_register` (`rt/host_macos/reactor.saw:111-119`, `EV_ADD|EV_ONESHOT`, `udata = token`); the consumer `rt_reactor_poll` (`reactor.saw:158-193`) stores 0 through `udata` at `:177-181`.
- blocking offload (`_emit_blk_call`): registration `coro_transform.py:7900-7904` FIRST, then `_suspend_to(-1)` `:7905` → `__wake` store `:6742-6743` — EXPOSED (reproduced).
- reactor io park (`io_wait`/`io_wait_until`: accept/read/write/connect/signal): registration `:6983-6987` FIRST, `_suspend_to(-1)` `:6989` — EXPOSED (reproduced).
- nested `Pending` propagation (every embedded sub-frame): `pending_body` COPIES `sub.__wake` → `self.__wake` at `:8140-8143`, after the arm, once per frame — THE DOMINANT CLOBBER (codex's chain had 4 frames; the repro stalls at depth 2).
- outside-frame `io_wait` (sync caller, `codegen/calls.py:593-596`): registration first but token = 0 (poll skips null udata; poll-until-ready) — not exposed.
- sleep/timer: no registration, countdown in `remaining` (`taskgroup.saw:1616-1626`) — not exposed.
- channel `receive` (design 230): level-triggered re-READ of the readiness word (`__park_flag_set`, `taskgroup.saw:363-366`) + 1 ms re-scan — self-healing, not exposed.
- cancel wake: independent of the wake word (`__park_io_runnable`, `:340-342`) — which is why `cancel()` still frees a clobbered task. `join`: condvar + broadcast — not exposed.
SECONDARY FINDING (doctrine): the arm IGNORES `kevent`'s return at `reactor.saw:105, 118, 142, 150` and `__saw_exec_io_register` returns `Void`, so a failed arm is structurally unreportable and presents exactly as this bug.

## Fixes tried in scratch compiler copies (tracked tree untouched)
Fix A = park word stored BEFORE the arm at both lowerings (`_suspend_to(write_wake=False)` after). Fix B = B1 `__saw_exec_io_register` stamps -1 through the token before arming (guarded `token != 0`), so every readiness store is strictly later than the park store; B2 the nested propagation MERGES instead of copying (`if sub.__wake != -1 { self.__wake = sub.__wake }`; other wake reasons and deadlines propagate unchanged).

| build | proc offload | net park |
|---|---|---|
| baseline | 11 / 256 | 4 / 96 |
| Fix A | 5 / 128 (no improvement) | 9 / 96 (no improvement) |
| Fix B | 0 / 384 | 0 / 96 |

FIX A ALONE DOES NOT FIX IT — both repro shapes park one frame below the root, so the propagation copy re-creates the clobber after A fixed the leaf. 28 park-exercising examples (net_serve_*, net_precise_*, net_two_concurrent_parked_reads, channel_*, sleep_seam_multi_chunk, offload_*, process_output_multithreaded/concurrent, process_cancel_during_child, net_cancel_parked_mt, signal_concurrency_pins, …) compile + run with BYTE-IDENTICAL stdout on base, A and B (no suite run). Probe D (detect without preventing: stamp -1 before the arm, print `SL353-CLOBBER` when the propagation is about to overwrite a 0 with a stale -1, then do it anyway): proc 1/1 stalled runs, 0/127 clean; net 39/39 stalled, 0/57 clean (probe D's extra store inflates the net rate — a within-D correlation; the cross-build claim is baseline stalls vs fix B's 0/480).

## Earlier flakes
Not confirmable locally (runner history has three stamps, no stall records; battery logs on this host are Sep 1-8). Structurally the exposed battery lane is irdet (`devtools/irdet/src/main.saw:74` `DEFAULT_JOBS = 8`, `:779` `TaskGroup(threads: opts.jobs)`, `Command.output()` at `:255/:418/:486` — thousands of children per `--all`); the suite's exposure is weak (`process_output_multithreaded.saw` is `threads: 2`, two children: 0 stalls in 96 oversubscribed runs). Rate ≈ 1 stall per ~10⁴ offloads at 4× oversubscription, ~0 when not oversubscribed.

## Not covered
No suite/battery/irdet; no lldb memory proof on an own stall (attach exceeded 300 s — the in-process watchdog + probe D substitute); Linux/epoll not probed (the compiler-side stores are host-independent; no evidence); `Task.spawn` not built separately (the `threads=1` control covers the cooperative engine); depth-4 chain not built (depth 2 stalls; deeper widens the window).
